Commentary.Commentary: We are back with India's reply and the all-important chase of this tournament. The players are already out in the middle now. Kamalini G and Trisha Gongadi are the two openers for India Women Under-19. Nthabiseng Nini to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, with just 89 runs to chase, India Women Under-19 will fancy their chances of defending their title. South Africa, on the other hand, will need to produce something truly special with the ball to turn this game around. Early wickets will be key, and they’ll have to bring their A-game in the field to create pressure from the get-go. Chase in a bit!

India Women Under-19 have put one foot firmly on the podium, with a dominant display of spin bowling in the grand finale. The slow bowlers were at their ruthless best, claiming 9 out of 10 wickets. Aayushi Shukla was sensational upfront, returning figures of 4-2-9-2, applying relentless pressure with her accuracy. Trisha Gongadi led from the front, picking up three crucial wickets, while Parunika Sisodia and Vaishnavi Sharma took two wickets each, adding to India’s stranglehold. With her two wickets today, Vaishnavi Sharma has officially finished as the tournament's highest wicket-taker, unless South Africa’s Kayla Reyneke produces an improbable spell in the second innings.

Shabnam of India Women Under 19 is up for a quick chat. She says that she is very happy that they have planned to bowl out them under 80. Adds that the fourth and sixth could be crucial so the skipper backed her to bowl those overs. Mentions that she knew that Jemma would go to charge her on that last ball and thus she changed the line and dragged the length. Says that she believes that the batters will chase it down and they will become again champions.

From there, India’s spin stranglehold tightened. Skipper Kayla Reyneke found herself trapped at the crease, struggling to rotate the strike as the pressure built from both ends. South Africa crumbled to 44/5 by the 13th over, unable to break free. A glimmer of resistance came from Mieke van Voorst and Fay Cowling, who stitched together a 30-run partnership, offering brief hope. But India’s bowlers came roaring back, dismantling the remaining lineup with ease. From 74/5, South Africa lost their last five wickets for just 8 runs, collapsing to 82 all out at the end of 20 overs.

Jemma Botha started aggressively, finding a few crisp boundaries in the opening over against pace. However, Indian skipper, Niki Prasad quickly assessed the situation and introduced spin, which paid immediate dividends. The breakthrough came swiftly, and soon after, Botha too was sent back, dealing a huge early blow to South Africa, especially considering the importance of their opening pair in this tournament.

Sheer dominance from India in the first innings! The Indian spinners once again proved their class, weaving a web that the South African batters simply couldn’t escape from. Opting to bat first on the big stage, South Africa are bundled out for just 82 runs, a total well below par in this high-stakes final.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS! India Women Under-19 have squeezed up runs here completely and maintained the pressure right from the start. They have already taken three wickets halfway down the inning and will want to take more in the coming overs to make this game one-sided. On the other hand, South Africa Women Under-19 are clearly struggling even to rotate the strike here as their skipper Kayla Reyneke has come out to the crease and struggled to find the timing. They will need to regroup and find a way out of this scrappy phase to score some runs and push to at least a good defendable total. An interesting game of play is ahead of us.

Diara Ramlakan lunges to block but plays for the turn and gets beaten on the inside edge. The ball brushes off her front pad and rattles into the stumps. South Africa Women Under-19 are 20/3.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! What a catch behind the wickets to dismiss the in-form batter Jemma Botha! India Women Under-19 have taken two wickets inside the Powerplay already and both openers are back in the hut for South Africa! She is caught up at the crease as she manages to get only an outside edge that goes to the right of the keeper. Kamalini G reacts quickly as she dives to her right and takes a one-hand stunner. South Africa Women Under-19 are 20/2.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match formalities! And it comes down to just two now. We are all ready for the ICC U-19 Women's T20 World Cup Final. The atmosphere is great and the crowd are buzzing here in Kuala Lumpur. The India Women Under-19 players are in a huddle where Niki Prasad is giving a last-minute pep talk. Then they spread out to take their respective field positions. Jemma Botha and Simone Lourens are the two openers for South Africa Women Under-19. Joshitha V J has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

We are moments away from the start of the final, but before that the volunteers bring out the national flags for both countries. The two umpires walk out and pick up the match ball. They are followed by the players from both sides who line up for their respective national anthem. It will be India's first followed by the national anthem of South Africa.

Kamalini G of India Women Under-19 also shares a few words. She says that she just kept it simple and played every ball on its merit. Adds that she has played the South African team in the tri-series and knows about what the spinners and pacers will bowl and she is ready. Ends by saying that it is very tough to be here but she is very excited to be a part of this final.

Karabo Meso of South Africa Women Under-19 is up for a quick chat. She says that it has been amazing as they were working hard before the final and this is the day finally after practising for 18 months or so. Adds that looking back on the series against India, she learned so much and she is ready to play against them. Mentions that the senior players have been around for a while and they have tried to take one game at a time and just enjoy the time in the middle and don’t think much about ahead.

PITCH REPORT - Charles Dagnall is at the middle for the pitch analysis. He says there a slight breeze across the ground and it's 33 degrees in the middle at the moment. Mentions that the square boundaries are 54 meters and 55 meters while the straight boundary is 66 meters and the batters will have to push those deep fielders and turn runs around. Says the pitch is very hard and will play similarly to the Semi-Finals and the batters will need to play straight while bowlers will have to target the stumps and not offer width. Concludes that 140 or 150 could be a par score.

Niki Prasad, the captain of India Women Under-19, says that the weather and pitch are looking good and they just want to come out and give their 100 percent when they bowl. Adds that it is a very special moment for them to play in the final as they were waiting for this day. Mentions that they have grit in the group and they knew in the semi-final that England would put some pressure on them. Says that there are some nerves but they want to remain calm. Informs that there are no changes.

Kayla Reyneke, the skipper of South Africa Women Under-19 says they just want to put runs on the board and take it from there. Adds that this is their first final and they are excited and ready to go. Mentions that they have a few standout performers but cricket is a team sport and they will have to come good as a team.

India Women Under-19 (Unchanged Playing XI) - Kamalini G (WK), Trisha Gongadi, Sanika Chalke, Niki Prasad (C), Ishwari Awasare, Mithila Vinod, Shabnam, Aayushi Shukla, Vaishnavi Sharma, Joshitha V J, Parunika Sisodia.

South Africa Women Under-19 (Unchanged Playing XI) - Jemma Botha, Simone Lourens, Diara Ramlakan (in for Luyanda Nzuza), Kayla Reyneke (C), Karabo Meso (WK), Mieke van Voorst, Fay Cowling, Seshnie Naidu, Ashleigh van Wyk, Monalisa Legodi, Nthabiseng Nini.
TOSS - South Africa Women Under-19 have won the toss and elected to BAT first in this big final.

Both teams have their strengths, but India looks like the more settled unit with in-form batters and a lethal bowling attack. The pitch is expected to be a good surface for batters, making powerplay overs crucial for both sides. The weather is expected to be overcast and we have a reserve day but we hope rain stays away so that we can get a full match. With everything on the line, expect a cracking contest under the Kuala Lumpur sky. Don’t go anywhere as the toss and playing XI are just moments away!

South Africa Women Under-19 have fought their way into the final with gritty performances. Their captain, Kayla Reyneke, has led from the front, contributing with both bat and ball. Jemma Botha has been their leading run-scorer with 89 runs, including a crucial 37 in the semifinal. Their strength, however, lies in their all-rounders, with Monalisa Legodi and Reyneke making valuable contributions. In the bowling attack, Reyneke with 10 wickets and Legodi with 6 wickets have been South Africa’s key weapons, with the latter delivering a match-winning 4/4 in the semifinal. The Proteas will need their top order to fire early and provide a solid foundation against India’s potent bowling lineup.

India Women Under-19 have been the team to beat this tournament, winning all their games with commanding performances. Their top order has been in sublime touch, led by Trisha Gongadi, who has amassed 265 runs in six matches at a blistering strike rate so far in this tournament, including a century. Kamalini G has also played a crucial role, scoring 135 runs with a healthy average. In the bowling department, Vaishnavi Sharma has been lethal, picking up 15 wickets at an astonishing economy of under 3, including a five-wicket haul. Aayushi Shukla and Parunika Sisodia have also chipped in consistently. However, India will want their middle order to step up in case of early wickets, and all eyes will be on their spinners to control the game in the middle overs.

It’s time for the grand finale of the ICC Women’s Under-19 T20 World Cup 2025, set to take place at Bayuemas Oval, Kuala Lumpur! Hello and welcome, the stage is set for a thrilling clash between India Women Under-19 and South Africa Women Under-19, both undefeated so far and hungry for glory. India Women Under-19 have met South Africa Women Under-19 just once in the T20 World Cup, which was in the previous edition and breezed past them with a dominant performance. They are on red-hot form this season as well and will want to carry the momentum ahead and will be desperate to repeat history as defending champions. However, South Africa have shown immense growth and resilience, winning all their games and proving they can handle high-pressure situations. Their semifinal victory wasn’t as straightforward as India’s, but it highlighted their ability to fight till the end, a quality that will be crucial in this high-stakes encounter. With two in-form teams, some of the tournament’s best performers on the show, and the ultimate prize on the line, we are set for an epic showdown!
... MATCH DAY ...

We have finally arrived at the summit clash of the ICC Women's Under-19 T20 World Cup 2025, where from 16 teams, only two remain and are ready to battle it out for the coveted trophy. It’s the grand finale, and fittingly, the two best teams of the tournament, both unbeaten, are set to lock horns. South Africa Women Under-19 will take on the defending champions, India Women Under-19, at the Bayuemas Oval in Kuala Lumpur, with the ultimate bragging rights at stake. Both teams have been dominant throughout the tournament, dismantling opponents with ease. However, South Africa’s semi-final clash against Australia was arguably their toughest challenge yet, where, for the first time, they had to battle through a full contest. Their previous matches had either been wrapped up in a hurry against lower-ranked teams or cut short by rain, but when it mattered most, they played like a well-oiled machine, stunning an Australian side that was a strong contender for the final. Jemma Botha and Simone Lourens have been the pillars of their top order, consistently providing runs, while the middle order, previously untested, stood up in the semis, with Kayla Reyneke and Karabo Meso delivering crucial performances. On the bowling front, Kayla Reyneke has been outstanding, and the resurgence of Ashleigh van Wyk in the semi-final will provide a significant boost. South Africa have ticked all boxes but will need to be at their absolute best against an Indian side in red-hot form. India Women Under-19 have been a beacon of consistency, with both their batting and bowling units firing on all cylinders, racking up convincing wins game after game. Trisha Gongadi, the tournament's leading run-getter, has been exceptional at the top, alongside Kamalini G, who sits third on the run charts. The top three batters have done most of the damage, though the middle order has chipped in effectively when required. But it’s India’s bowling attack that has truly set them apart. Their spinners have been ruthless, with Vaishnavi Sharma leading the wicket charts, closely followed by Aayushi Shukla, highlighting the sheer dominance of India’s slow bowlers. While the spinners have been phenomenal, the pace attack has been equally effective in the early overs, consistently applying pressure and making the ball talk. On paper, India look like the favourites, with an all-round squad that has been there, done that, and knows how to win big tournaments. But South Africa have match-winners who have stepped up at the right moments and will be hoping to do so one last time against the tournament's strongest force. Memories of the 2024 Men’s T20 World Cup clash between these two nations remain fresh, where India snatched victory from the jaws of defeat - could we be in for another similar edge-of-the-seat thriller? South Africa will be eager to get their hands on the trophy, capping off a brilliant period for their cricket, while India will leave no stone unturned to defend their crown. It’s all set for an electrifying finale!
